title: Application Discovery Questionnaire
overview: This 10-question framework helps define clear requirements for any software project. Answer these questions to align stakeholders and guide development decisions.

questions.question: What problem does your application solve, and who feels that pain the most?
questions.why: Defines the core value proposition and primary users.
examples: Dog-walkers struggle to track multiple clients; my app will auto-schedule routes for walkers with >10 dogs per day.
University students can't find last-minute study rooms; the app aggregates real-time room availability.

questions.question: On which devices and platforms should the first version run?
questions.why: Narrows the tech stack and design constraints.
examples: iOS and Android phones only—tablets and desktop later.
Any modern browser; must work on low-end Chromebooks.
Desktop VR headset (Meta Quest 3) plus a slim companion mobile app.

questions.question: Which scripting/programming language(s) do you prefer, and why?
questions.why: Aligns with existing team skill, hosting options, and library ecosystems.
examples: Python – "Rapid prototyping, huge AI libraries, fine if server-side only."
JavaScript/TypeScript – "Runs in browsers and Node.js, single language front-to-back."
Kotlin – "Modern, null-safe; I expect tight Android integration."
No strong preference—recommend what fits my budget.

questions.question: List the must-have features for the MVP (Minimum Viable Product)?
questions.why: Prevents scope creep; anchors the first release.
examples: User login with Google, basic profile, create/read/update/delete notes, and share a note via link.
GPS route tracking, step counter, calorie estimate, and weekly summary email.
Upload 1-minute video, auto-generate captions, allow simple trim, then publish.

questions.question: Which third-party services or APIs should we integrate with (if any)?
questions.why: Determines licensing cost, data flow, and potential vendor lock-in.
examples: Stripe for payments, Google Maps for geocoding, Twilio for SMS.
No external APIs; everything must run offline (military use-case).
OpenAI for text generation + Cloudinary for media storage.

questions.question: How should data be stored and synced?
questions.why: Guides database choice, offline strategy, and security controls.
examples: Cloud-only, PostgreSQL on Supabase.
Real-time collaboration—need Firebase Firestore-style live updates.

questions.question: What level of security, privacy, or compliance is required?
questions.why: Impacts architecture, hosting region, and audit features.
examples: Must be HIPAA-compliant; patient data encrypted in transit and at rest.
Consumer social app—standard OAuth, no special compliance.
European customers only—GDPR data-deletion workflow mandatory.

questions.question: How should the user interface feel (style, tone, accessibility)?
questions.why: Sets design language and accessibility targets.
examples: Minimalistic, monochrome, like Notion; AA accessibility at least.
Playful neon cyber-punk with motion effects; WCAG can be AA except AAA contrast not needed.
Enterprise dashboard: dense tables, light mode only, Excel import vibes.

questions.question: What are your performance or scalability expectations for the first year?
questions.why: Determines hosting tier, caching, and cost planning.
examples: Pilot with 500 beta users; uptime 99% is fine.
Expect viral spikes—handle 100k concurrent users for live trivia.
Internal tool for 50 employees—latency under 1s, nothing fancy.

questions.question: Budget, timeline, and post-launch maintenance — what's realistic?
questions.why: Aligns scope with resources and clarifies ongoing responsibilities.
examples: $15k MVP budget, 3-month build, then $500/month for updates.
Open-source passion project—volunteer devs, slow timeline.
VC-backed: up to $250k this year, need v1 in 10 weeks, full-time dev retainer after.

next_steps: Document Requirements → Drop answers into a shared doc and distill into functional + non-functional requirements
Design Architecture → Sketch an architecture and tech stack diagram that satisfies Q2–Q7
Create Roadmap → Derive a phased roadmap from Q4, Q9, and Q10
Validate → Confirm with the client before writing any code
deliverables_checklist: User interface mockups or style guide

note: Structured mirror of the canonical prose. All question text, why-lines, and example answers are copied verbatim. The canonical markdown remains the single source of truth.
